# APX Data Dictionary

*APX Specification · APX 0.14.0 · OpenAPI 0.14.0 · built on APDS 4.1 (2026-01-14) · Draft*

## Introduction

This data dictionary gives the definitions and characteristics of every
class, attribute, association role, enumeration and external code list
that the APX API defines. It is generated from the normative OpenAPI
document, `spec/dist/apx-v1.yaml`, each time the documents are built, so
it always matches the API.

It follows the layout of the APDS 4.1 Data Dictionary:

- **A.1** is ordered by package. APX has one package per module. Each
  package lists its classes, specializations, associations and
  attributes.
- **A.2** lists the datatypes.
- **A.3** lists the enumerations alphabetically.
- **A.4** lists the external code lists (APX registries) with every entry.
- **Annex B** lists the APDS 4.1 classes APX carries, and says where the
  APX overlay adds to or corrects them.
- **Annex C** links each APX class to the data element proposed from it
  to APDS.

APDS 4.1 classes are not redefined here. Where an APX member uses one,
its type names the APDS domain and class (for example
`Session.Session`), and its definition is in the APDS 4.1 Data
Dictionary.

### How to read the tables

The tables use the columns of the APDS 4.1 Data Dictionary, with three
additions for APX:

1. **Class name:** the symbolic name (UpperCamelCase) of the class, as
   it appears in the OpenAPI document.
2. **Association end / Attribute name:** the symbolic name of the member.
   A member of an unnamed structure is written `owner.member`.
3. **Designation:** the name in natural language.
4. **Definition:** the definition, taken from the OpenAPI document. Where
   the document gives none, the definition of the referenced class is
   used, or the wording APX uses for the same member elsewhere. A
   definition marked ‡ was derived from the member's name because the
   API gives no description. A definition marked † was written by the
   editors from the APX standard text because the API gives none. Both
   marks show where the OpenAPI descriptions should be filled in, so that
   a later edition can drop the marks. An enumeration value shown with
   "—" has no definition yet.
5. **Kind:** `class`, `union` (one of several shapes) or `enumeration`.
6. **Multiplicity:** written m..n, as in APDS. m is 0 for optional and 1
   or more for mandatory; n is a number or `*`.
7. **Target / Type:** the class, datatype or enumeration of the member,
   written `Domain.Name` for APDS 4.1 types and `Package.Name` for APX
   types. "code list" names the APX registry whose values the member
   takes.
8. **Notes (APX):** `read-only` (set by the server), `write-only`
   (accepted on input, never returned), `nullable` (may be sent as null)
   and `deprecated`.
9. **APDS status (APX):** `APX only` when the class stays in the APX
   specification, or the APDS element proposed from it and its tier (see
   06 Requests to APDS).

## A.1 Data dictionary of packages for "APX"

### A.1.1 "Common" package

**A.1.1.1 Location of "Common" package.** The location of the "Common" package is:

`-- APX/Common` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/common/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Parts 4, 5, 10 and 12)

**A.1.1.2 Classes of the "Common" package**

*Table A.1 -- Classes of the "Common" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ApxResourceCore | Apx resource core | Identity core shared by every APX-defined resource. Shaped so any APX resource can itself be the target of an APDS Reference or VersionedReference (RFC 4122 UUID identifier + integer version). | class | APX only |
| CodeListValue | Code list value | A value drawn from an APX or implementer UserDefinedCodeList — carries the defined value plus an optional ReferencedCodeListEntry-style pointer to the list that defines it. | class | APX only |
| CredentialDigest | Credential digest | The `apds-ext:apx:credential-digest@1.0` decoration (Part 9 §9.6 rule 6): a keyed digest of a normalized credential identification (a plate), so a consumer that only needs "same plate?" can match without the plate itself. `value` is base64url(HMAC-SHA-256(key, normalized identification)); the key is named by `keyId` and distributed through `GET /v1/digest-keys`. Visible under `apx.data:read`. | class | APX only |
| EventEnvelope | Event envelope | The single envelope for all APX asynchronous delivery (webhooks and SSE). Attribute names are aligned with CloudEvents 1.0 (informative mapping in the standard's annex); `subject` carries an APDS Reference so events bind to APDS/APX entities natively. | class | APX only |
| Extensions | Extensions | The official APDS extension container (Use Case Document §C.2.5). Keys MUST follow `apds-ext:<namespace>:<class>@<major>.<minor>`. Implementations MUST preserve unknown extension keys on round-trip (tolerant reader, faithful writer). An APX decoration key, wherever the container appears, MUST carry a value valid against that decoration's schema (Part 4 §4.3); other keys are any object. | class | APX only |
| Problem | Problem | RFC 9457 problem details. APX problem `type` URIs are registered in the APX problem-type registry. Used for all APX error responses; APDS-native routes may alternatively use the APDS ResponseStatus shape. | class | APX only |
| RecordInfo | Record info | Provenance metadata for an APX resource, aligned to the APDS Information Model's RecordType (creationTime/creator/lastUpdate). All timestamps are RFC 3339 (APDS DateTime). | class | Proposed: RecordType (Tier 3) |

There are no specializations in the "Common" package.

This is that flag — and because it rides inside the RateTable, every consumer mirroring the deck through the native `/rates` route (Part 5 §5.2) receives it with the table, no second query. APX deliberately defines NO selection rules here (length of stay, time of day, caller type): the system presenting the deck to an agent or a third party applies its own guardrails. The server's only rule is enforcement — a pushNegotiatedRate naming a table that is not flagged negotiable is refused (422 rate-not-negotiable). | 0..1 | Control.RatePolicy |  |

Every field optional; each recognized attribute carries its own confidence. APDS's `vehicleAncillaryIdentification` (country, stateProvince, make, model, color) remains the APDS-visible copy of the winning values; this block adds the per-attribute confidence, the candidates that lost, and the passage geometry APDS has no fields for. | 0..1 | Lpr.LprReadDetail |  |

Facing is relative to the facility, not to the lane's mode, so it holds on `reversible` lanes. Describes the setup only; APX derives nothing from it. | 0..1 | Lpr.LaneCameras |  |

| Extensions | apds-ext:apx:match-evidence@1.0 | 0 | How a link to a Session was established and how sure it is (Part 5 §5.8; shared by the `matches[]` member of `apds-ext:apx:session-detail@1.0` and the decoration `apds-ext:apx:match-evidence@1.0` on a Violation or ValetTicket). Visible under `apx.data:read`. | 0..1 | Common.CredentialDigest |  |

Generated at build time (tools/change-payloads.mjs); the generic ChangePayload remains the shape of change-feed items. | class | APX only |
| MatchEvidence | Match evidence | How a link to a Session was established and how sure it is (Part 5 §5.8; shared by the `matches[]` member of `apds-ext:apx:session-detail@1.0` and the decoration `apds-ext:apx:match-evidence@1.0` on a Violation or ValetTicket). Carries no plate characters and no vehicle attribute values (Part 9 §9.6). Where both ends of one link carry evidence (the Session's `matches[]` entry and the decoration on the Violation or ValetTicket), the two MUST agree. Evidence with `plate.method: lenient` or `applied: false` may excuse a stay but never accuse one: `issue` on a Violation resting on it is 409 `violation-not-issuable` (Part 19 §19.4 rule 5). | class | Proposed: MatchEvidence (Tier 3); Proposed: MatchTypeEnum (Tier 3); Proposed: MatchDecisionEnum (Tier 3) |
| ObservationElementChangePayload | Observation element change payload | A change-mode body for native `PUT /observations/{id}` (Part 5 §5.1a): `id` plus only the ObservationElement members that changed; an absent member is unchanged and an explicit `null` clears it. Every member present is checked against the class, and a member the class does not define is refused. Generated at build time (tools/change-payloads.mjs); the generic ChangePayload remains the shape of change-feed items. | class | APX only |
| OccupancyHistoryPage | Occupancy history page | Occupancy per clock interval for one HierarchyElement (Part 5 §5.5a): the history behind the §5.5 snapshot, derived from the APDS DemandTable records the implementation holds. Buckets are aligned to the interval boundary in the place's time zone; a bucket with no demand record carries no counts, never a guess. | class | Proposed: DemandType (Tier 3) |
| OccupancySnapshot | Occupancy snapshot | Current occupancy for one HierarchyElement, computed from the APDS occupancy model (Supply + DemandTable) that natively lives in the Place hierarchy. A convenience READ (Part 5 §5.5): the Place payload remains the source of truth; this answers "how full is it right now" without pulling the hierarchy. Composed entirely of verbatim APDS occupancy classes — APX adds no parallel occupancy datatypes. | class | APX only |
| RateTableChangePayload | Rate table change payload | A change-mode body for native `PUT /rates/{id}` (Part 5 §5.1a): `id` plus only the RateTable members that changed; an absent member is unchanged and an explicit `null` clears it. Every member present is checked against the class, and a member the class does not define is refused. Generated at build time (tools/change-payloads.mjs); the generic ChangePayload remains the shape of change-feed items. | class | APX only |
| RightSpecificationChangePayload | Right specification change payload | A change-mode body for native `PUT /rights/specs/{id}` (Part 5 §5.1a): `id` plus only the RightSpecification members that changed; an absent member is unchanged and an explicit `null` clears it. Every member present is checked against the class, and a member the class does not define is refused. Generated at build time (tools/change-payloads.mjs); the generic ChangePayload remains the shape of change-feed items. | class | APX only |
| SessionChangePayload | Session change payload | A change-mode body for native `PUT /sessions/{id}` (Part 5 §5.1a): `id` plus only the Session members that changed; an absent member is unchanged and an explicit `null` clears it. Every member present is checked against the class, and a member the class does not define is refused. Generated at build time (tools/change-payloads.mjs); the generic ChangePayload remains the shape of change-feed items. | class | APX only |
| SessionClosure | Session closure | Why and how a Session ended (Part 5 §5.8). | class | Proposed: SessionClosure (Tier 1) |
| SessionDetail | Session detail | The `apds-ext:apx:session-detail@1.0` decoration on an APDS Session (Part 5 §5.8): what the pairing of reads decided and APDS has no members for — the reads behind the visit, why and how it ended, the matches it rests on, and the parent visit of an area Session. Written with the native Session POST/PUT by an external pairing engine; a server that pairs reads itself SHOULD write the same block on its own Sessions. A plain APDS client ignores it. It adds no event topic and carries no plate characters. A write that breaks a consistency rule of §5.8 is 422 and nothing is written. | class | Proposed: Session (Tier 1); Proposed: SessionLifecycleEnum (Tier 2) |
| SessionReadBinding | Session read binding | One LPR read attached to a Session by the pairing engine (Part 5 §5.8, member `reads[]` of `apds-ext:apx:session-detail@1.0`). | class | Proposed: SessionRead (Tier 1); Proposed: SessionReadRoleEnum (Tier 1) |

### A.1.4 "Events" package

**A.1.4.1 Location of "Events" package.** The location of the "Events" package is:

`-- APX/Events` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/events/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 8)

**A.1.4.2 Classes of the "Events" package**

*Table A.10 -- Classes of the "Events" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ApxEventSubscription | Apx event subscription | Superset of the APDS 4.1 EventSubscription. A stock APDS client sending only `{endpoint, topics}` (EventTypeEnum values) gets stock behavior; the APX fields are additive and optional. | class | APX only |
| ApxEventSubscriptionPatch | Apx event subscription patch | Body of `PATCH /webhooks/{id}`: a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) over ApxEventSubscription. Members present replace the stored value, an explicit `null` clears an optional member, and absent members are unchanged — so `{"status": "active"}` alone resumes a subscription. `version`, when given, is the precondition (Part 4 §4.2a); a stale one is 409 `version-conflict`. `id`, `activeKeyIds`, and `recordInfo` are server-managed and cannot be patched. | class | APX only |
| DeliveryAttempt | Delivery attempt | One delivery attempt of one event to one subscription. | class | APX only |
| DeliveryRecord | Delivery record | One entry in a subscription's delivery ledger. | class | APX only |
| SubscriptionFailure | Subscription failure | Data of `apx.subscription.failed.v1` (Part 8 §8.3): which subscription stopped, where it was delivering, and the attempt that exhausted the schedule. The envelope `subject` references the same subscription. | class | APX only |
| SubscriptionFilters | Subscription filters | Server-side delivery filtering. | class | APX only |

**A.1.4.3 Specializations of the "Events" package**

There are no specializations in the "Events" package.

### A.1.5 "Control" package

**A.1.5.1 Location of "Control" package.** The location of the "Control" package is:

`-- APX/Control` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/control/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 6)

**A.1.5.2 Classes of the "Control" package**

*Table A.13 -- Classes of the "Control" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approval | Approval | Approval evidence, REQUIRED on a write whose AllowedAction said requiresApproval (Part 17 §17.3). Servers MUST reject a requires-approval action without it (403 approval-required). One shared shape for control commands and domain actions (e.g. refunds). | class | APX only |
| Command | Command | A request for an operational action against a lane/device/place. Perishable (expiryTime), idempotent (Idempotency-Key), fully audited (immutable statusHistory). | class | APX only |
| CommandResult | Command result | The structured outcome of a command, populated by the server when the command reaches `succeeded` (Part 6 §6.1a) and absent before then. Members are normative per command type: `lostTicket` → `ticketNumber`, `session`, `amountDue`; `matchTicket` → `session`, `amountDue`; `pushNegotiatedRate` → `amountDue`, and `rateTable` when a table was selected (absent for a stated amount, which the lane inquiry reports as `currentTicket.negotiatedAmount`). Other command types leave it absent unless a registry entry says otherwise. It restates what the lane inquiry shows, so a console can continue (print, take payment) without parsing `statusHistory[].detail` or making a second call. | class | APX only |
| DeviceStatus | Device status | Live state overlay keyed by Reference to an APDS SupplementalEquipment — never duplicates its descriptive fields. APDS 4.1 has no general equipment status list: its RefillPointStatusEnum (Data Dictionary A.3.53) covers refill points only and is absent from apds-api-4.1.yaml. deviceState values come from the APX registry apx-device-states, which follows that enumeration's style and shares its available, occupied, inoperative and unknown values. Attachable to APDS payloads as apds-ext:apx:devicestatus@1.0. | class | Proposed: EquipmentStatus (Tier 1) |
| LaneStatus | Lane status | The transaction context at a lane right now (the call-center screen-pop). Composes APDS references and data; adds no parallel entities. | class | APX only |
| MatchCandidate | Match candidate | An open session at the place that plausibly belongs to the vehicle in the lane (Part 6 §6.7). Produced by the lane inquiry from the lane's own LPR read, a presented credential, the account registry (by plate or phone), or a checked-in reservation. Composes APDS references; adds no parallel session store. Advisory until a matchTicket command binds one. | class | APX only |
| RatePolicy | Rate policy | Level B decoration on an APDS RateTable, carried in its `extensions` container as `apds-ext:apx:ratepolicy@1.0` (Part 6 §6.6). APDS models the rate deck completely; it has no way to say which tables an agent may offer as a negotiated rate. This is that flag — and because it rides inside the RateTable, every consumer mirroring the deck through the native `/rates` route (Part 5 §5.2) receives it with the table, no second query. APX deliberately defines NO selection rules here (length of stay, time of day, caller type): the system presenting the deck to an agent or a third party applies its own guardrails. The server's only rule is enforcement — a pushNegotiatedRate naming a table that is not flagged negotiable is refused (422 rate-not-negotiable). | class | Proposed: RateTable (Tier 2) |
| ValidationProvider | Validation provider | A venue/organisation allowed to validate tickets at a place. | class | APX only |

### A.1.8 "Lpr" package

**A.1.8.1 Location of "Lpr" package.** The location of the "Lpr" package is:

`-- APX/Lpr` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/lpr/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 13)

**A.1.8.2 Classes of the "Lpr" package**

*Table A.22 -- Classes of the "Lpr" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AttributeRead | Attribute read | One recognized attribute with its own confidence (0–1, APDS Confidence scale). | class | Proposed: AttributeRead (Tier 1) |
| LaneCameras | Lane cameras | The LPR cameras on a lane and which way each one faces (Part 13 §13.3a(5)). Carried on an APDS VehicularAccess as the Level B decoration `apds-ext:apx:lane-cameras@1.0` in its `extensions` container (Part 4 §4.3). Facing is relative to the facility, not to the lane's mode, so it holds on `reversible` lanes. Describes the setup only; APX derives nothing from it. | class | Proposed: VehicularAccess (Tier 2); Proposed: LaneCamera (Tier 2); Proposed: CameraFacingEnum (Tier 2) |
| LprRead | Lpr read | One plate read joined with its ticket/session context. | class | Proposed: ImageTypeEnum (Tier 2) |
| LprReadDetail | Lpr read detail | What a modern LPR camera knows beyond the plate string and one overall score (Part 13 §13.3a). Carried on the ingested APDS Observation as the Level B decoration `apds-ext:apx:lpr-read@1.0` in its `extensions` container (Part 4 §4.3 — plain APDS consumers ignore it), and projected on `LprRead.detail` and `PlateCandidate.detail`. Every field optional; each recognized attribute carries its own confidence. APDS's `vehicleAncillaryIdentification` (country, stateProvince, make, model, color) remains the APDS-visible copy of the winning values; this block adds the per-attribute confidence, the candidates that lost, and the passage geometry APDS has no fields for. | class | Proposed: ObservationElement (Tier 1); Proposed: AlternateRead (Tier 1); Proposed: ReadReview (Tier 2); Proposed: Image (Tier 2); Proposed: ImageRegion (Tier 2); Proposed: ReadAttributeEnum (Tier 1); Proposed: VehicleMovementEnum (Tier 1); Proposed: PlateFaceEnum (Tier 2); Proposed: ReadReviewStateEnum (Tier 2) |
| LprReadSearch | Lpr read search | Request body of `POST /v1/lpr/reads:search` (Part 13 §13.3): the same keys as the `GET` lookup, carried in a body so a plate never enters a URL that proxies and access logs keep (Part 9 §9.6). At least one of `plate`, `ticket`, `observation`, or `session` is REQUIRED. | class | APX only |
| PlateCorrection | Plate correction | Request body of `PUT /v1/lpr/reads/{observation}/plate` (Part 13 §13.3a(4a)): a reviewer's decision on one read. `confirmed` keeps the engine's values; `corrected` replaces them with the ones given; `rejected` marks the read unusable for pairing and enforcement. `plate`, `country`, and `stateProvince` belong to `corrected` only: sent with another decision they are 422 `request-unprocessable`. | class | APX only |

**A.1.8.3 Specializations of the "Lpr" package**

There are no specializations in the "Lpr" package.

### A.1.9 "Reservations" package

**A.1.9.1 Location of "Reservations" package.** The location of the "Reservations" package is:

### A.1.11 "Violations" package

**A.1.11.1 Location of "Violations" package.** The location of the "Violations" package is:

`-- APX/Violations` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/violations/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 19)

**A.1.11.2 Classes of the "Violations" package**

*Table A.31 -- Classes of the "Violations" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EligibilityResult | Eligibility result | "Is this vehicle entitled to be here right now?" — the guided-enforcement screen-pop (Part 19 §19.3). A convenience READ composed from the APDS entities that natively answer the question: AssignedRights (APDS's own enforcement source of truth), Sessions, and reservation/permit profiles. Adds no parallel entitlement entity; the AssignedRight remains authoritative. | class | APX only |
| EnforcementPolicy | Enforcement policy | The jurisdictional rules that govern issuing and escalating violations at a place (Part 19 §19.10): lawful notice delivery per detection mode, the initial penalty cap, the escalation schedule, windows, and whether posted signage is required. Bound to a HierarchyElement with subtree inheritance — the nearest ancestor's policy applies unless a descendant overrides it. A machine-readable summary an operator configures from the governing statute; never the statute itself. Edits use versioned `PUT` with the version last read as `If-Match` or body `version` (Part 4 §4.2a; 409 `version-conflict` when stale). | class | Proposed: EnforcementPolicy (Tier 2); Proposed: NoticeDeliveryRule (Tier 2); Proposed: PenaltyLimit (Tier 3); Proposed: EscalationStep (Tier 2) |
| Signage | Signage | A record of what is posted at a place — the text, a photo, the sign's position, and when it was in force (Part 19 §19.11). Bound to a HierarchyElement with subtree inheritance. Versioned so an appeal can show the sign as it stood on the day: superseding a sign is a new version or a new record with `effectiveTo` set, never an edit in place of historical text. Edits use versioned `PUT` (Part 4 §4.2a). | class | Proposed: Signage (Tier 2); Proposed: SignTypeEnum (Tier 2) |
| Violation | Violation | An enforcement finding against a vehicle at a place: the detection (automated, guided, or manual), the eligibility check that justified it, the evidence, the issued notice/citation, settlement, and any appeal — with the immutable lifecycle audit (Part 4 §4.2). | class | Proposed: Violation (Tier 1); Proposed: Notice (Tier 1); Proposed: Appeal (Tier 2); Proposed: ViolationStatusEnum (Tier 1); Proposed: NoticeKindEnum (Tier 1); Proposed: NoticeDeliveryMethodEnum (Tier 1); Proposed: AppealReasonEnum (Tier 2); Proposed: AppealResolutionEnum (Tier 2) |
| ViolationAppealOpen | Violation appeal open | Request body opening an appeal on an issued violation, or on a paid one within the policy's appeal window (pay-then-appeal). | class | APX only |
| ViolationAppealResolution | Violation appeal resolution | Request body resolving an open appeal. | class | APX only |
| ViolationAppliedPayment | Violation applied payment | One payment applied to a violation (Part 19 §19.6a): a partial payment or the settling one. `payment` references the Part 13 record (APDS Payment or APX PaymentRecord) when the money moved through this server; a payment an import source took itself (§19.13) may carry only the source's own `reference`. | class | APX only |
| ViolationDetection | Violation detection | How and when the candidate was found. | class | Proposed: ViolationDetection (Tier 1); Proposed: DetectionModeEnum (Tier 1) |
| ViolationEvidence | Violation evidence | Evidence media, as access-controlled LINKS (Part 9 §9.6 — never inline). Each item points at an APDS Image reachable under the same authentication and place grant as this resource. | list | APX only |
| ViolationImport | Violation import | Request body of `POST /v1/enforcement/violation-imports` (Part 19 §19.13): a violation as an external enforcement system reports it — in any state, with the `statusHistory[]` times the source recorded, the notice, the amounts and payments, and the `apds-ext:apx:violation-source@1.0` decoration that keys it. The members mean what they mean on `Violation`; the difference is that `violationStatus`, `notice`, `amountPaid`, `payments`, and `statusHistory` are written by the caller here, because the source, not this server, decided them. A state at or past issuance (`issued`, `paid`, `appealed`, `closed`) REQUIRES `notice` (with `noticeNumber` and `issuedTime`) and `amount` (400 `invalid-request` otherwise); `paid` with `amountPaid` below `amount` is 422 `request-unprocessable`. A warning with no fine is `issued` (or `closed`) with `notice.noticeKind` `warning` and a zero `amount`. | class | APX only |
| ViolationIssue | Violation issue | Request body issuing the notice/citation for a confirmed (or, under automated policy, detected) violation. | class | APX only |
| ViolationLocation | Violation location | Where the violation was observed and from where — modelled on the APDS Observation `Location` shape (Part 19 §19.9), with two differences: `observerLocation` is optional here (APDS requires it; an automated finding copied from a fixed sensor may have none), and `accuracyMetres` is added. The member names and the `PointLocation` types are APDS's own. GeoJSON positions are [longitude, latitude] in that order; enforcement tools that store latitude first MUST swap on the wire. Automated detections SHOULD copy this from the underlying Observation. | class | APX only |
| ViolationPaymentAttachment | Violation payment attachment | Request body attaching a Payment to an issued violation. The full amount (or the remainder) settles it (`paid`); a smaller `amount` is a partial payment (Part 19 §19.6a) that stays `issued`. | class | APX only |
| ViolationReview | Violation review | Request body for guided-enforcement review — confirm or dismiss a detected candidate. | class | APX only |
| ViolationSessionLink | Violation session link | Request body of `POST /v1/violations/{id}/session` (Part 19 §19.13): sets, corrects, or clears `relatedSession` after creation, carrying the match evidence. `session: null` clears the link. `If-Match` carries the Violation version last read. | class | APX only |
| ViolationSource | Violation source | The `apds-ext:apx:violation-source@1.0` decoration (Part 19 §19.13): a violation issued by an external enforcement system and imported through `POST /v1/enforcement/violation-imports`, keyed on `system` + `recordId`. `sourceRevision`, or without one `sourceUpdatedTime`, orders the source's revisions. | class | APX only |
| ViolationVehicle | Violation vehicle | The credential observed on the vehicle (an APDS CredentialTypeEnum credential). | class | APX only |
| ViolationVoid | Violation void | Request body voiding a violation (terminal; never deletes the audit). | class | APX only |

### A.1.12 "Validations" package

**A.1.12.1 Location of "Validations" package.** The location of the "Validations" package is:

`-- APX/Validations` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/validations/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 20)

**A.1.12.2 Classes of the "Validations" package**

*Table A.34 -- Classes of the "Validations" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ValidationBenefit | Validation benefit | What a validation is worth. Exactly one of `amount` (money off), `duration` (comped time, valued at the applicable rate), or `percentage` (proportionate discount — the APDS RateDiscount `discountRate` semantics) applies; `description` is always present so agents can answer disputes in plain language. A program body whose benefit carries none or more than one of the three is refused with 422 `request-unprocessable` (Part 20 §20.1); the rule is stated here rather than as a schema `oneOf` so that existing request bodies keep validating. | class | Proposed: ValidationBenefit (Tier 2) |
| ValidationInstrument | Validation instrument | The current state of one validation code — the pay-station / merchant-app "is this code good?" read. | class | Proposed: ValidationInstrument (Tier 2); Proposed: ValidationInstrumentStatusEnum (Tier 2) |
| ValidationIssuance | Validation issuance | A batch of validation instruments issued to a program — printed codes, QR codes, stamp stock, digital tokens. `codes[]` is returned EXACTLY ONCE, in the creation response (the webhook-secret convention, Part 8 §8.1); later reads omit it. `stamp` and `api` batches carry no codes. | class | Proposed: ValidationIssuance (Tier 2); Proposed: ValidationIssuanceMethodEnum (Tier 2); Proposed: ValidationIssuanceStatusEnum (Tier 2) |
| ValidationIssuanceRequest | Validation issuance request | Request body for `POST /v1/validations/programs/{id}/issuances`: the writable members of `ValidationIssuance`. The program is the one the path names; `program` MAY be repeated in the body, and a value that differs from the path is 422 `request-unprocessable` (Part 20 §20.2). Server-assigned members (`id`, `version`, `codes`, `issuanceStatus`) are ignored if sent. | class | APX only |
| ValidationProgram | Validation program | A merchant's enrolment to validate parking at a place: who the provider is, what the validation is worth, the rules that bound it, how the merchant is billed, and how instruments are issued. Active programs ARE the source of the Part 6 `GET /v1/validations/providers` list when `apx-validations` is claimed. | class | Proposed: ValidationProgram (Tier 2); Proposed: ValidationRules (Tier 2); Proposed: ValidationBilling (Tier 3); Proposed: ValidationBillingModelEnum (Tier 3); Proposed: ValidationBillingCycleEnum (Tier 3) |
| ValidationRedemption | Validation redemption | One validation applied to one ticket/session — the ledger entry every channel writes: a pay station scanning a code, a merchant app, an agent's `applyValidation` command (Part 6), or a lane device. `validationId` is the APDS `Segment.validationId`, so APDS consumers see the same redemption without speaking APX. `amountReduced` is the ACTUAL value removed from the amount due (dispute evidence), never the nominal benefit. | class | Proposed: ValidationRedemption (Tier 1); Proposed: ValidationRedemptionStatusEnum (Tier 1) |
| ValidationRedemptionReversal | Validation redemption reversal | Request body reversing a redemption (wrong ticket, merchant dispute, fraud). | class | APX only |
| ValidationStatement | Validation statement | A program's redemptions and billable total for a period. Returned as a computed preview by `GET …/statement`, and as an IMMUTABLE record once a period is closed by `POST …/statements` (`statementStatus: closed`; the operator's accounting system invoices from it). Closed periods MUST NOT overlap (409 `statement-overlap`). | class | APX only |
| ValidationStatementClose | Validation statement close | Request body closing a billing period for a program. | class | APX only |
| ValidationVoid | Validation void | Request body voiding an issuance batch or a single instrument code (Part 20 §20.2 rule 5) — a stolen sheet, a leaked code, a misprint. | class | APX only |
| ValidationVoidDetail | Validation void detail | Who voided an issuance or instrument, when, and why. Present once `void`. | class | APX only |

**A.1.12.3 Specializations of the "Validations" package**

There are no specializations in the "Validations" package.

### A.1.13 "Credentials" package

**A.1.13.1 Location of "Credentials" package.** The location of the "Credentials" package is:

`-- APX/Credentials` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/credentials/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 21)

**A.1.13.2 Classes of the "Credentials" package**

*Table A.37 -- Classes of the "Credentials" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AccessEvent | Access event | One access attempt at a lane, whether or not the presented credential matched a CredentialRecord — the item of `GET /v1/access-events` and the data of `apx.credentials.access.v1`. `credential` is REQUIRED whenever a record matched; it is absent only for `denialReason: unknownCredential`, where `presented` is REQUIRED instead (Part 21 §21.4). Every `CredentialAccessEvent` is a valid `AccessEvent`; this schema exists because `CredentialAccessEvent.credential` is required and relaxing it would break clients of the per-credential history. | class | Proposed: AccessEvent (Tier 1); Proposed: AccessOutcomeEnum (Tier 1) |
| CredentialAccessEvent | Credential access event | One access attempt with a credential at a lane — granted or denied, and why. Fills the gap that APDS EventTypeEnum has no access events (published as `apx.credentials.access.v1`). | class | APX only |
| CredentialRecord | Credential record | One access credential — keycard, fob, RFID tag or transponder, mobile credential, hangtag, or a plate used as the credential — with its holder, validity, physical media, and lifecycle. `credentialType` is the APDS read technology; `media.form` is the physical form. | class | Proposed: CredentialAssigned (Tier 1); Proposed: CredentialMedia (Tier 1); Proposed: CredentialSuspension (Tier 1); Proposed: CredentialStatusEnum (Tier 1); Proposed: CredentialMediaFormEnum (Tier 1); Proposed: DepositStatusEnum (Tier 1) |
| CredentialReplaceRequest | Credential replace request | Request body issuing a successor credential. The new record inherits holder, account, assigned rights, places, and validity unless overridden; the old record becomes `replaced` and is removed from the APDS AssignedRights at the same instant the successor is materialized. | class | APX only |
| CredentialTransition | Credential transition | Request body for activate / suspend / resume / report-lost / revoke. | class | APX only |
| PresentedCredential | Presented credential | What the reader actually read at the lane. Carried on an access event when no CredentialRecord matched (`denialReason: unknownCredential`), and MAY be carried otherwise. Personal data under Part 21 §21.5: returned only under `apx.credentials:*` scopes. | class | Proposed: PresentedCredential (Tier 1) |

There are no specializations in the "Credentials" package.

### A.1.16 "Resolution" package

**A.1.16.1 Location of "Resolution" package.** The location of the "Resolution" package is:

`-- APX/Resolution` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/resolution/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 17)

**A.1.16.2 Classes of the "Resolution" package**

*Table A.46 -- Classes of the "Resolution" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AllowedAction | Allowed action | One policy decision about one action, evaluated for THIS context, THIS credential, and THIS moment (Part 17 §17.3). The server — never the consuming agent, human or AI — decides permissibility. Approval requirements are policy-dependent, which is why they live here at runtime and not in a registry. | class | APX only |
| OverrideRecord | Override record | A recent manual override relevant to this context (courtesy exits, gate opens, passback resets…). Summarizes a Part 6 Command. | class | APX only |
| PassbackStatus | Passback status | Anti-passback state overlay for one APDS Credential. | class | APX only |
| PlateCandidate | Plate candidate | One candidate plate read for correction workflows (Part 17 §17.5) — a projection over APDS Observations, imagery as access-controlled links (Part 9 §9.6). | class | APX only |
| ResolutionContext | Resolution context | The aggregated customer-service context (Part 17): everything the server could resolve about one interaction, plus the policy-decided allowed actions. Every section beyond the required core is OPTIONAL — implementations include what they know and omit what they don't (graceful degradation), and MUST NOT include sections the caller's scopes/grants could not read directly. | class | APX only |
| ResolutionIssue | Resolution issue | The machine-classified issue this context describes. `code` is a definedValue from the apx-issue-types registry (open, per Part 11); `display` is the human-readable summary shown to agents. | class | APX only |
| ResolutionResolveRequest | Resolution resolve request | Whatever PARKING-DOMAIN identifiers are currently known — the server resolves every relationship it can (Part 17 §17.2). At least one IDENTIFYING member is required — `device`, `place`, `lane`, `session`, `holder`, `credential`, `plate`, `ticketNumber`, or `reservationCode`; all are optional individually. `interactionId`, `correlationId`, and `channel` are correlation metadata and do not count: a body without an identifying member is 400 `invalid-request` (Part 17 §17.1). Unknown members are ignored (tolerant reader) and never used for resolution. (`minProperties: 1` is the only part of this rule the schema states; the full rule is enforced by the server.) | class | APX only |
| SupportInteraction | Support interaction | One customer-service interaction (human or AI agent), recorded so future resolution contexts can surface "they called twice yesterday". | class | Proposed: SupportInteraction (Tier 3); Proposed: SupportAgentTypeEnum (Tier 3) |

There are no specializations in the "Resolution" package.

### A.1.17 "Charging" package

**A.1.17.1 Location of "Charging" package.** The location of the "Charging" package is:

`-- APX/Charging` (source: `spec/openapi/domains/charging/schemas.yaml`; normative text: APX Part 23)

**A.1.17.2 Classes of the "Charging" package**

*Table A.49 -- Classes of the "Charging" package*

| Class name | Designation | Definition | Kind | APDS status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ChargingBayPresence | Charging bay presence | Part 23 — what the bay in front of a charging point physically contains, as observed by an overhead camera, a ground sensor, the charger's own connector state, or an attendant — fused by the server (Part 23 §23.3). Distinguishes the cases the charger alone cannot: a vehicle parked in the bay but not plugged in (an ICE vehicle, or an EV not charging), and a bay blocked by something that is not a vehicle. Also the request body a camera analytics system POSTs to `…/points/{id}/bay`. | class | Proposed: ChargingBayPresence (Tier 3); Proposed: BayPresenceEnum (Tier 3); Proposed: BayPresenceSourceEnum (Tier 3) |
| ChargingEvent | Charging event | Part 23 — one physical-timeline event the charging-network bridge reports for a session — the APX counterpart of an OCPP 2.0.1 TransactionEvent. The server applies the lifecycle transition (Part 23 §23.2) and appends `statusHistory`. `meterValue` events update `energy` without a state change. Idempotent by `Idempotency-Key` (bridges retry). | class | APX only |
| ChargingPaymentAttachment | Charging payment attachment | Part 23 — request body attaching the settling payment to an `unplugged` `directPayment` session, or recording the network's charge detail record for a `chargingNetwork` one. | class | APX only |
| ChargingPointStatus | Charging point status | Part 23 — live state overlay keyed by Reference to an APDS ElectricChargingEquipment — the dynamic counterpart of the static ElectricChargingPoint (APDS `refillPointIndex` exists precisely "to link static and dynamic publications"). Never duplicates the static descriptive fields (connector types, power ratings live in APDS). Carries availability per point and per connector, the current session, a reservation, and what the bay camera sees. Same pattern as Part 6 DeviceStatus. Also the request body the charging-network bridge PUTs to `…/points/{id}/status`. | class | Proposed: ChargingPointStatus (Tier 3); Proposed: ConnectorStatus (Tier 3) |
| ChargingSession | Charging session | Part 23 — one charge of one vehicle at one charging point, as the parking system sees it: who was authorized and how, the timeline from plug-in to unplug, energy delivered, the idle period after charging completed, cost, and how it settles — while the APDS Session remains the parking stay and is only referenced. The charging network's own identifiers (OCPP transaction, OCPI session/CDR) ride along opaquely so the two records can be reconciled without APX redefining either protocol. | class | Proposed: ChargingSession (Tier 3); Proposed: ChargingCost (Tier 3); Proposed: ChargingIdleTerms (Tier 3); Proposed: ChargingSessionStatusEnum (Tier 3); Proposed: ChargingStopReasonEnum (Tier 3); Proposed: ChargingSettlementModeEnum (Tier 3) |

**A.1.17.3 Specializations of the "Charging" package**

There are no specializations in the "Charging" package.

## A.2 Data dictionary of datatypes for "APX"

APX uses the APDS 4.1 datatypes where a member carries APDS content. The types below are how this dictionary names the JSON types of APX members.

*Table A.52 -- Datatypes*

| Datatype | Definition | Nearest APDS 4.1 datatype |
| --- | --- | --- |
| String | A sequence of characters. | String |
| Integer | A whole number. | Integer |
| Decimal | A decimal number. | Decimal / Real |
| Boolean | true or false. | Boolean |
| DateTime | An instant, written per RFC 3339 with a UTC offset. | DateTime |
| Date | A calendar date, written per RFC 3339 (full-date). | Date |
| Uuid | A universally unique identifier per RFC 9562, used as a record id (Part 4). | String (identifier) |
| Url | A URI per RFC 3986. | Url |
| Email | An e-mail address. | Email |
| Map of T | A JSON object whose keys are free text and whose values are of type T. | — |
| Structure | An unnamed group of members. Its members are listed under the owning class as owner.member. | — |
| Object | Any JSON object; its content is set by the referenced specification or by an extension. | — |

### A.3.7 The <<D2Enumeration>> "ApxEventSubscription.status"

`active` delivers; `paused` holds matching events for up to 24 hours and delivers them in order on resume (Part 8 §8.1); `failed` is server-assigned when the retry schedule is exhausted (a client setting it is 400 `invalid-request`). PATCH `status: active` to resume a paused or failed subscription.

Defined inline on `ApxEventSubscription`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

*Table A.59 -- Values contained in the enumeration "ApxEventSubscription.status"*

| Enumerated value name | Designation | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| active | active | The subscription delivers matching events. † |
| paused | paused | The client has paused delivery; matching events are held for up to 24 hours and delivered in order on resume (Part 8 §8.1). † |
| failed | failed | The retry schedule was exhausted; the server set this state and delivery stops until the client resumes the subscription (Part 8 §8.1). † |

### A.3.16 The <<D2Enumeration>> "ChargingPointStatus.availability"

Point-level availability (the busiest connector wins): `available`; `occupied` — a cable is connected but no energy is flowing (plugged in, suspended, complete, or idle); `charging`; `reserved` (Part 14 AssignedRight in force); `blocked` — the bay is occupied or obstructed without a connected cable (from `bay.presence`); `inoperative` (planned: maintenance, closed hours); `outOfOrder` (fault); `unknown`. Aligned with the OCPI EVSE status vocabulary.

Defined inline on `ChargingPointStatus`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

| occupied | occupied | a cable is connected but no energy is flowing |
| charging | charging | Energy is flowing on the point (Part 23 §23.1). † |
| reserved | reserved | Part 14 AssignedRight in force |
| blocked | blocked | the bay is occupied |
| inoperative | inoperative | planned: maintenance, closed hours |
| outOfOrder | out of order | fault |
| unknown | unknown | The point's state is not known. † |

### A.3.64 The <<D2Enumeration>> "PaymentRecord.captureStatus"

Whether an approved payment's funds have been collected (Part 13 §13.1a). `authorized` = a hold: the payment layer approved an authorization-only request (`captureLater: true`), funds are held, nothing is collected yet; settled by `POST /v1/payments/{id}/capture` or released by `…/void`. `captured` = collected. Absent = `captured` (a sale). A hold is returned to the caller that created it, but is not listed by `GET /v1/payments` unless asked for, is not published on `apx.accounts.payment.recorded.v1`, and is not materialized as an APDS Payment until captured.

Defined inline on `PaymentRecord`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

*Table A.116 -- Values contained in the enumeration "PaymentRecord.captureStatus"*

| Enumerated value name | Designation | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| authorized | authorized | a hold: the payment layer approved an |
| captured | captured | collected |

### A.3.65 The <<D2Enumeration>> "PaymentRecord.channel"

Where the payment was captured. `lane` = a lane device; `payStation` = a pay-on-foot or pay station; `agent` = a person on the implementer's own PCI-scoped terminal; `autoAttendant` = a PCI-compliant IVR that captures the card out of band; `online` = web or mobile app. APX never carries PANs, whichever channel is used.

Defined inline on `PaymentRecord`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

| agent | agent | a person on the implementer's |
| autoAttendant | auto attendant | a PCI-compliant IVR that |
| online | online | web or mobile app |
| other | other | The payment was captured through a channel not otherwise listed. † |

### A.3.75 The <<D2Enumeration>> "SessionDetail.lifecycle"

`open` — a vehicle is in the facility, no `actualEnd` yet; `ended` — closed, may still be revised; `final` — no further revision expected; `disputed` — under review. Every state but `open` requires `actualEnd`, and `open` forbids it (422 `request-unprocessable` otherwise). `final` is the writer's statement, never a lock: a server MUST NOT refuse a later revision on that ground.

Defined inline on `SessionDetail`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

| ended | ended | closed, may still be revised |
| final | final | no further revision |
| disputed | disputed | under review |

### A.3.102 The <<D2Enumeration>> "Violation.appeal.openedFrom"

The state the appeal was opened from; `paid` is a pay-then-appeal (Part 19 §19.6). `upheld` and `reduced` return the violation to this state.

Defined inline on `Violation`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

*Table A.154 -- Values contained in the enumeration "Violation.appeal.openedFrom"*

| Enumerated value name | Designation | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| issued | issued | The appeal was opened while the violation was issued and unpaid. † |
| paid | paid | The appeal was opened after payment, a pay-then-appeal (Part 19 §19.6). † |

### A.3.103 The <<D2Enumeration>> "Violation.violationStatus"

Current lifecycle state (see schema description for transitions).

Defined inline on `Violation`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

*Table A.155 -- Values contained in the enumeration "Violation.violationStatus"*

| Enumerated value name | Designation | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| detected | detected | The violation has been found and is awaiting review. † |
| confirmed | confirmed | A reviewer has confirmed the violation and a notice may be issued. † |
| dismissed | dismissed | A reviewer has rejected the violation; this is final. † |
| issued | issued | A notice has been issued and payment is outstanding. † |
| paid | paid | The amount has been paid in full. † |
| appealed | appealed | An appeal is open. † |
| closed | closed | The violation is finished, after payment or a successful appeal; this is final. † |
| voided | voided | The violation was withdrawn, for example as issued in error or a duplicate; this is final (Part 19 §19.1). † |

### A.3.104 The <<D2Enumeration>> "ViolationDetection.mode"

`automated` — a camera/sensor pipeline created the violation with no human in the loop. `guided` — the system surfaced a candidate (typically to a handheld) and an officer confirms on site. `manual` — an officer created the violation directly.

Defined inline on `ViolationDetection`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

*Table A.156 -- Values contained in the enumeration "ViolationDetection.mode"*

| Enumerated value name | Designation | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| automated | automated | a camera/sensor pipeline created the violation with |
| guided | guided | the system surfaced a candidate |
| manual | manual | an officer created the violation directly. |

### A.3.105 The <<D2Enumeration>> "ViolationImport.violationStatus"

The APX state the source's status maps to. `paid` requires `amountPaid` at least `amount`; a part-paid violation is `issued` (Part 19 §19.6a). The source's own wording goes in the decoration's `sourceStatus`.

Defined inline on `ViolationImport`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

*Table A.157 -- Values contained in the enumeration "ViolationImport.violationStatus"*

| Enumerated value name | Designation | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| detected | detected | The source reports the violation as found and awaiting review. † |
| confirmed | confirmed | The source reports the violation as confirmed by a reviewer, with no notice yet. † |
| dismissed | dismissed | The source reports the violation as rejected by a reviewer; this is final. † |
| issued | issued | Part 19 §19.6a |
| paid | paid | The source reports the amount as paid in full (Part 19 §19.6a). † |
| appealed | appealed | The source reports an open appeal. † |
| closed | closed | The source reports the violation as finished; this is final. † |
| voided | voided | The source reports the violation as withdrawn; this is final. † |

### A.3.106 The <<D2Enumeration>> "ViolationReview.decision"

Values of decision on ViolationReview.

Defined inline on `ViolationReview`; the API names it by its owner and attribute.

*Table A.158 -- Values contained in the enumeration "ViolationReview.decision"*

| Enumerated value name | Designation | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| confirm | confirm | The reviewer confirms the detected candidate as a violation. † |
| dismiss | dismiss | The reviewer dismisses the detected candidate. † |

## A.4 External code lists for "APX"

These lists extend APX string members without changing the schema, in the same way as the APDS user-defined code lists (APDS Use Case Document, Annex D). Implementers may publish further values (Part 11).

### A.4.1 External code list "apx-access-denial-reasons"

Used by: `LaneStatus.monthlyCredential.denialReason`, `CredentialAccessEvent.denialReason`, `AccessEvent.denialReason`. Seeds the APDS proposal AccessDenialReasonEnum (Tier 1). Published as an APDS `UserDefinedCodeList` at `spec/registries/apx-access-denial-reasons.json` (Part 11).

*Table A.159 -- Entries in the code list "apx-access-denial-reasons"*

| definedValue | Description |
| --- | --- |
| credentialSuspended | The presented credential matched a CredentialRecord that is suspended. |
| credentialLost | The presented credential matched a CredentialRecord reported lost. |
| credentialRevoked | The presented credential matched a CredentialRecord that is revoked. |
| credentialReplaced | The presented credential matched a CredentialRecord that has been replaced by another. |
| credentialExpired | The presented credential matched a CredentialRecord that has expired. |
| unknownCredential | The presented value matched no CredentialRecord; the event carries what the reader read. |
| passback | Denied by anti-passback state (the credential is already in, or already out); corrected through the Part 17 passback commands. |
| accountBalance | Denied because of the holder's outstanding balance or account status. |
| outsidePlace | The credential is valid, but not at this place. |
| outsideValidity | The credential is valid at this place, but not at this time. |
| credentialNotYetActive | The presented credential matched a CredentialRecord that is issued but not yet active (its validity has not started, or it awaits activation). Distinct from outsideValidity, which is an active credential presented outside its permitted times. |

### A.4.2 External code list "apx-alert-types"

Used by: `SubscriptionFilters.alertTypes`. Seeds the APDS proposal AlertTypeEnum (Tier 2). Published as an APDS `UserDefinedCodeList` at `spec/registries/apx-alert-types.json` (Part 11).

*Table A.160 -- Entries in the code list "apx-alert-types"*

| definedValue | Description |
| --- | --- |
| noCheckOut | Vehicle/right shows no check-out for a completed stay (APDS Use Case C.2.2 transaction exception). |
| wrongSpace | Vehicle occupies a different space than reserved/checked-in (C.2.2 transaction exception). |
| occupiedWithoutCheckIn | Space occupied with no matching check-in/session (C.2.2 space status). |
| iceInEvSpace | Non-EV vehicle occupying an EV charging space (C.2.2 transaction exception). |
| overstay | Session exceeds its right's validity or maximum stay. |
| deviceFault | A device reports a fault state. |
| deviceOffline | A device stopped communicating (lastCommunication exceeded threshold). |
| laneBlocked | A lane is blocked (vehicle stuck, barrier obstruction). |
| occupancyThresholdExceeded | Occupancy demand crossed a configured threshold for a place element. |
| paymentException | A payment failed, was reversed, or requires attention. |
| intercomRequest | A customer requested assistance at a lane/device intercom. |
| webhookDeliveryFailed | A subscription exhausted its delivery retry schedule and was marked failed (self-referential alert). |
| wrongWayTravel | An operator-defined alert that a vehicle travelled against a lane's configured purpose (e.g. entered on an exit lane). APX does not raise it or define when it applies: LPR reads carry only the vehicle's accessEvent, and the lane used does not change it (Part 13 §13.3a(6)). |
| evBayNotCharging | A vehicle has occupied an EV charging bay without connecting beyond the place's grace — the EV counterpart of iceInEvSpace, derived from the Part 23 §23.3 bay-presence fusion; the camera Observation is the evidence. |
| evBayBlocked | An EV charging bay is obstructed by something other than a parked vehicle (cones, debris, a straddling vehicle), derived from the Part 23 §23.3 bay-presence fusion; the camera Observation is the evidence. |
| watchListArrival | A credential on a watch plate list (Part 24) was read at a place where the list has alertOnArrival; relatedEntity is the PlateListEntry, the read is the evidence. |
| scofflawArrival | A credential on a scofflaw plate list (Part 24) was read at a place where the list has alertOnArrival; relatedEntity is the PlateListEntry. |
| refusedServiceArrival | A credential on a plate list with refuseService arrived at a lane and service was refused (the refused-service sign shown, the gate not vended); relatedEntity is the PlateListEntry, the displayMessage command's result.display is the proof of display. |

### A.4.3 External code list "apx-command-types"

Used by: Not referenced by a schema description. Published as an APDS `UserDefinedCodeList` at `spec/registries/apx-command-types.json` (Part 11).

*Table A.161 -- Entries in the code list "apx-command-types"*

| definedValue | Description |
| --- | --- |
| vendGate | Open (vend) a gate/barrier at the target lane once for one vehicle. |
| holdGateOpen | Hold the gate/barrier at the target lane open until released by a subsequent setDeviceState or closeLane command. |
| closeLane | Close the target lane to further entries/exits. |
| lostTicket | Issue a lost-ticket transaction at the target lane using the lost-ticket method given in parameters. |
| pushRate | Apply the RateTable referenced in parameters to the target lane or place. |
| applyValidation | Apply a validation from the given validation provider to the ticket/session referenced in parameters. |
| setDeviceState | Request the target device transition to the state given in parameters. |
| displayMessage | Display the message given in parameters on the target device (VMS, lane display). |
| restartDevice | Restart (reboot) the target device. |
| resetPassback | Reset the anti-passback state of the credential referenced in parameters to normal. |
| forceIn | Force the credential referenced in parameters to recorded presence 'inside' (passback correction). |
| forceOut | Force the credential referenced in parameters to recorded presence 'outside' (passback correction). |
| courtesyExit | Vend the gate at the target lane as a tracked courtesy exit for the account/holder referenced in parameters — counted against courtesy policy. |
| pushNegotiatedRate | Apply a negotiated rate to the CURRENT ticket at the target lane only, never to the lane's deck: a negotiable RateTable in parameters.rateTable, or (negotiatedAmounts feature) any amount in parameters.amount with a reason. The command's agent is who set it. |
| matchTicket | Bind the current transaction at the target lane to the open Session referenced in parameters (ticket matching), pricing the exit from that session's true entry time; the command's agent is who made the match. |
| startCharging | Remote-start charging on the target ElectricChargingEquipment for a plugged-in vehicle whose own authorization failed; parameters connectorIndex and chargingSession (Reference), or an authorization object for the server to open one (Part 23 §23.9). |
| stopCharging | Remote-stop charging on the target ElectricChargingEquipment; parameters connectorIndex and chargingSession; the bridge reports chargingEnded with stopReason remote (Part 23 §23.9). |
| unlockConnector | Release a cable the target ElectricChargingEquipment will not let go of; parameter connectorIndex; physicallyConfirmed only when the charger reported the connector unlocked or the bay camera saw the cable move (Part 23 §23.9). |

### A.4.4 External code list "apx-conformance-classes"

Used by: Not referenced by a schema description. Published as an APDS `UserDefinedCodeList` at `spec/registries/apx-conformance-classes.json` (Part 11).

*Table A.162 -- Entries in the code list "apx-conformance-classes"*

| definedValue | Description |
| --- | --- |
| apx-data | Implements APDS 4.1 native data routes with the APX data profile (Full/Change, tombstones, cursor change feed). |
| apx-events | Implements the APX delivery fabric over APDS /webhooks with HMAC signing and the normative retry schedule. |
| apx-events-sse | Implements the SSE event stream with Last-Event-ID resume. |
| apx-control | Implements the command plane, lane inquiry, validations, and device status. |
| apx-alerts | Implements the alert resource and lifecycle. |
| apx-discovery | Implements credential-scoped capability discovery. |
| apx-accounts | Implements account lookup, take-payment, and accounting write-back. |
| apx-payment-history | Implements payment history lookup by ticket. |
| apx-lpr | Implements LPR plate/ticket cross-lookup over APDS Observations. |
| apx-reservations | Implements the reservations profile over APDS quotes and assigned rights. |
| apx-permits | Implements the permits profile over RightSpecification, RightPool, and Credential. |
| apx-tolling | Implements TollTransaction and its dispute lifecycle. |
| apx-mtls | Optional hardening: mutual TLS on all APX endpoints. |
| apx-resolution | Implements Customer Service & Resolution: resolution contexts, policy-decided allowed actions, passback status, plate candidates, and support-interaction history. |
| apx-violations | Implements enforcement: the Violation lifecycle (automated and guided detection, review, issuance, settlement, appeals, void) and the eligibility check. |
| apx-validations | Implements validation program management: merchant enrolment, instrument issuance, the redemption ledger, and closable billing statements; the Part 6 provider list derives from active programs. |
| apx-credentials | Implements credential lifecycle: issue, activate, suspend, resume, report lost, revoke, replace, access-event history; active records materialized as APDS CredentialAssigned on the holder's AssignedRights. |
| apx-valet | Implements valet custody: drop-off with condition evidence, parked position and keys, the retrieval queue with ETA, staging, verified handback, and the customer request scope. |
| apx-charging | Implements the parking-side view of EV charging: live charging-point status with bay-presence fusion, the ChargingSession referencing the APDS Session, idle after complete, three settlement modes, and the customer status scope. Requires the base classes; the charger-control commands (Part 23 §23.9) require apx-control. |
| apx-plate-lists | Implements plate lists: watch, scofflaw, allow, and enforcement-vehicle lists with per-place flags, their entries, the change feed on both, and the apx.platelists.changed.v1 topic. Requires the base classes. |

### A.4.15 External code list "apx-violation-types"

Used by: `Violation.violationType`, `EligibilityResult.suggestedViolationType`, `ViolationSource.violationCode`, `ViolationImport.violationType`. Seeds the APDS proposal ViolationTypeEnum (Tier 1). Published as an APDS `UserDefinedCodeList` at `spec/registries/apx-violation-types.json` (Part 11).

*Table A.173 -- Entries in the code list "apx-violation-types"*

| definedValue | Description |
| --- | --- |
| noValidRight | No AssignedRight or paid Session covers the vehicle at the place at the observed time. |
| expiredRight | The nearest AssignedRight or Session covering the vehicle has ended (overstay past the paid/permitted time). |
| notYetValidRight | The vehicle's right exists but its validity has not started (early arrival on a reservation or future-dated permit). |
| wrongPlace | The vehicle holds a right for a different HierarchyElement (wrong zone, level, lot, or space). |
| maximumStayExceeded | The stay exceeds the place's maximum-stay operating restriction regardless of payment. |
| restrictedSpace | The vehicle occupies a space it is not eligible for (accessible, EV charging, loading, reserved, permit-only). |
| permitMisuse | A permit or credential is presented by a vehicle it was not issued to, or is suspended, cloned, or otherwise invalid. |
| noParkingPeriod | The vehicle is parked during a period when the place is closed to parking (street cleaning, event closure, tow-away window). |
| obstruction | The vehicle obstructs a lane, access, exit, hydrant, or another space. |
| other | A violation class not otherwise listed; the notice text carries the specifics. |
| chargingBayIdle | A vehicle remained connected in an EV charging bay after charging completed beyond the posted idle limit (Part 23 §23.10); evidenced by the ChargingSession and the bay Observation. |
